faqs.a:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this division, shall have the
               meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates
               a different meaning:
Alarm system
means any device designed for the detection of an unauthorized entry on or into any
               building, place or premises, or for alerting others of the commission of an unlawful
               act, or both, and when activated causes an audible and/or visual signal or transmits
               a signal or message to which police officers are expected to respond or that would
               imply to a reasonable person that police officers are needed at the alarm source to
               investigate a criminal activity or emergency. Included are single and/or multiple
               devices, such as an electronic unit which plugs directly into a 110-volt AC line.
Exception:
(1)
Single unit smoke detectors or personal protection alerting devices which alert only
                  the user and which do not require special wiring.
(2)
Alarms installed in or on motorized vehicles.
Alarm user
means any person, firm, business, partnership, association or corporation or employee
               thereof which maintains control of, his responsibility for, and/or is associated with
               the operation of the alarm device or who buys and/or leases or otherwise obtains or
               uses an alarm system.
False alarm
means an alarm signal necessitating response by the police department where a criminal
               activity does not exist.
Valid alarm
is where a criminal activity occurred, possibly occurred, or is occurring at the
               time of the alarm, as determined by the police officer's investigation.
(Code 1981, § 2-191(a); Ord. No. 1745, §§ 2—6, 5-18-1981; Ord. No. 1959, § 1, 8-1-1983;
               Ord. No. 3237, § 2, 12-18-1995)
